citations.quote:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in H$ write $v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1}\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=v_{\pi^{-1}(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n-1)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$ have a repeated factor, that is, $v_i=v_j$ for some distinct $i,j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, then $P_-(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=0$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of effects on $H$ as defined above, with $\sum_aF_a=I$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-$H$ calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $U:H\to K$ be a bijective linear map with
$$\langle Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle x,y\rangle_H\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in H .$$
Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_T$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and define
$$D(T'):=U D(T),\qquad T'(Ux):=U(Tx)\quad(x\in D(T)).$$
Then:

(a) $T'$ is well defined, linear, densely defined and self-adjoint on $K$;

(b) the assignment $E(B):=U E_T(B) U^{-1}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, and it is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$;

(c) for every unit vector $x\in H$ the scalar laws of the two operators agree,
$$\mu^{T'}_{Ux}(B):=\|E(B)Ux\|_K^2=\|E_T(B)x\|_H^2=:\mu^{T}_x(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel});$$

(d) $\sigma(T')=\sigma(T)$.

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]) and let
$S\in\mathcal B(H)$ be bounded. Then $ST$ and $TS$ are trace class and
$$\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\operatorname{tr}(TS) .$$
If $A,B\in\mathcal B(H)$ are Hilbert–Schmidt relative to a supplied Hilbert
basis $E$ of $H$ ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), then the products $AB$ and
$BA$ are trace class and
$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

**(a) State space.** Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] for a declared system of the declared massive-matter sector, with its assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. The **state space of the system in the model** is the set
$$D(H)=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}$$
of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]: the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $H$ of trace one. A **state** of the system is an element of $D(H)$; this is the geometry vocabulary for the general preparations of clause (iii) of the state postulate. The model's adopted assignment of a state to each preparation is not produced by this definition; it is the content of that postulate.

**(b) Pure and mixed states.** A state is **pure** when it is one of the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$, and **mixed** when it is not pure, as in [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the map
$$j:R(H)\to D(H),\qquad j([\psi])=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is a bijection of the ray space onto the set of pure states; and by clause (ii) of the state postulate the pure preparations are the unit rays of $H$, so the model's pure preparations are exactly its pure states.

**(c) State assigned to a state vector.** For a nonzero vector $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **state assigned to $\psi$** is the normalized rank-one operator
$$\widehat\rho(\psi)=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}\in D(H),$$
which by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; clause (ii) of the state postulate assigns the same operator to the pure preparation $[\psi]$. The zero vector is excluded here because $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ is defined only for $\psi\ne0$; no state is assigned to it, in agreement with the state postulate.

**(d) Mixtures and purity.** A **statistical mixture** of preparations with weights is the trace-norm convergent sum of clause (iii) of the state postulate; its value is the corresponding convex combination of states. The **purity** of a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})$, and by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]] a state is pure exactly when its purity equals $1$.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) record the readings of the state postulate in the geometry vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. The cited mathematical suppliers of the ray-to-state correspondence and of the purity criterion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is carried as a hypothesis of these readings. They adopt no assumption beyond the state postulate and that hypothesis, assert no dynamics, no probability law and no measurement model, and make no empirical claim: in particular, whether a given laboratory preparation is pure or mixed, and whether a given apparatus realizes a prescribed mixture, are physical identifications with uncertainty, governed by the preparation and apparatus assumptions of the framework, not consequences of this definition. Superselection restrictions and identical-particle symmetry sectors, where imposed, are separate assumptions by clause (v) of the state postulate and are not part of the state space fixed here.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

derivations.claim: [Invariance] Let $x,y\in\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$. By [F1] one has $U_\pi^{*}x=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)^{-1}x=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)x$ and likewise for $y$, so $\langle U_\pi\rho U_\pi^{*}x,y\rangle=\langle\rho U_\pi^{*}x,U_\pi^{*}y\rangle=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)^{2}\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle\rho x,y\rangle$ by the unitarity of $U_\pi$ and the sesquilinearity of the inner product. Every $U_\pi$ preserves the sector and, being unitary with inverse also preserving it, preserves its orthogonal complement: if $y$ is in that complement and $x$ is in the sector, $\langle U_\pi y,x\rangle=\langle y,U_\pi^*x\rangle=0$. The extended $\rho$ vanishes on the complement and maps into the sector, so the same holds for $U_\pi\rho U_\pi^*$. The established equality on the sector therefore gives $U_\pi\rho U_\pi^{*}=\rho$ on the entire labelled space; multiplying this identity on the left by $U_\pi^{*}$ and on the right by $U_\pi$ and using $U_\pi^{*}U_\pi=I$ gives $U_\pi^{*}\rho U_\pi=\rho$ as well. This proves (a).

[Sector-preserving case] Put $P:=P_\sigma^{(n)}$, $M:=\operatorname{ran}P$ and $A_\sigma:=A|_{D(A)\cap M}$. Under (c), [F3] gives $E_A(B)=U_\pi E_A(B)U_\pi^*$ for every $\pi$; hence $E_A(B)$ commutes with every $U_\pi$ and with their finite weighted sum $P$ from [F1]. Thus $E_\sigma(B):=E_A(B)|_M$ is a regular PVM on $M$: projections, products, normalization and strong countable additivity restrict from $E_A$, and its scalar measures at vectors of $M$ are unchanged. Also $APx=PAx$ for $x\in D(A)$ by the finite weighted sum and the domain equality $U_\pi D(A)=D(A)$. The domain $D(A)\cap M$ is dense in $M$, since projecting any ambient approximating sequence in $D(A)$ produces one in that domain. The restriction is self-adjoint: it is symmetric; if $y\in D(A_\sigma^*)\subset M$ and $z=A_\sigma^*y\in M$, then for every $x\in D(A)$, $\langle Ax,y\rangle=\langle APx,y\rangle=\langle Px,z\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle$. Therefore $y\in D(A^*)=D(A)$ and $Ay=z$, so $D(A_\sigma^*)\subseteq D(A_\sigma)$ and symmetry gives equality. For $x\in M$ the scalar second-moment domain and spectral integrals of $E_\sigma$ equal those of $E_A$, so [F2]'s uniqueness identifies $E_\sigma$ as the spectral PVM of $A_\sigma$. Finally the density expansion in clause (d) of [F1], $\rho=\sum_k w_k T_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm with $u_k\in M$, gives both traces as $\sum_k w_k\langle E_A(B)u_k,u_k\rangle$, since the zero extension uses the same vectors in the ambient space. Hence $\mu^{A_\sigma}_\rho(B)=\mu^A_\rho(B)=\mu^{A_\pi}_\rho(B)$, proving (c).

[Relabelled laws] Fix $\pi$ and an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$. Since $U_\pi$ is a bijective linear isometry of $H^{\otimes n}$ and $A$ is self-adjoint, [F3] gives that $A_\pi=U_\pi AU_\pi^{*}$ is self-adjoint on the domain $U_\pi D(A)$ with spectral measure $E_{A_\pi}(B)=U_\pi E_A(B)U_\pi^{*}$. Hence for every preparation $\rho$ and Borel $B$, $\mu^{A_\pi}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho U_\pi E_A(B)U_\pi^{*})$ by [F2]. Because $\rho$ is trace class and $U_\pi E_A(B)$ is bounded, [F4] applied twice gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho U_\pi E_A(B)U_\pi^{*})=\operatorname{tr}(U_\pi^{*}\rho U_\pi E_A(B))$; by step 1.1 the middle factor is $\rho$, so $\mu^{A_\pi}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\mu^{A}_\rho(B)$, which is (b) in the general form; for bounded $A$ the same computation with $A$ in place of $E_A(B)$ gives the displayed trace identity.

[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), step 2.1 proves (b) and step 1.2 proves (c). The proof uses only the adopted sector of P6, the readings of P1 and P2, and the cited spectral and trace mathematics under the declared choice hypotheses; no measured invariance, no dynamics and no species assignment is asserted.

citations.quote:
**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Let
$n\ge1$, and let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold completed tensor power with
$H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let
$P_\pm^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$, be the permutation
projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$
For $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, written $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$, put
$$e_J^\wedge:=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, e_{j_{\widehat{\sigma}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\widehat{\sigma}(n)}},$$
and for $\lambda\in W(n,d):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ put
$\operatorname{orb}(\lambda):=\{c\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n:|c|=\lambda\}$ and
$m_\lambda:=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$. Then:

(a) *product basis*: $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$H^{\otimes n}$, and $\dim H^{\otimes n}=d^n$;

(b) *Slater basis*: for every $J$ with $|J|=n$ one has
$e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ and the
family $(e_J^\wedge)_{J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\},\ |J|=n}$ is an orthonormal family whose
closed linear span is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$; it is therefore an
orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$,
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ when $n>d$. Moreover for every multi-index
$i$ one has $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ when two entries of $i$ coincide, and
$$P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\,\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$$
when the entries of $i$ are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J$ and
$\rho_i\in S_n$ is the unique permutation with $i_k=j_{\widehat{\rho_i}(k)}$;

(c) *symmetric basis*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is
nonzero, the family $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ is orthogonal,
$U_\pi m_\lambda=m_\lambda$ for every $\pi\in S_n$, and for every multi-index
$i$ there is a real number $\gamma_i>0$ with
$P_+^{(n)}(e_i)=\gamma_i\,m_{|i|}$; consequently
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is the linear span of $(m_\lambda)$, the family
$(m_\lambda)$ is an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$;

(d) *occupation operators*: for $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ the map
$$N_j:H^{\otimes n}\to H^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,e_i\rangle\,e_i,$$
is a self-adjoint bounded endomorphism, the $N_j$ commute pairwise,
$\sum_{j=1}^dN_j=nI$, and
$$N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)\,e_J^\wedge,\qquad N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_j\,m_\lambda .$$
Consequently both sectors are invariant under every $N_j$, the joint
eigenspaces of $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$ inside $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ are the
lines $\mathbb Ce_J^\wedge$ (one for each $n$-element subset $J$, with
eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$), and the joint eigenspaces inside
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (one for each
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$, with eigenvalue vector $\lambda$).

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt a declared species sector in the vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
the observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) The declared finite-mode model.** Fix $d\ge1$, a finite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $K$ of dimension $d$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with a
declared orthonormal basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, the **declared modes** of the
model, and an integer $n\ge1$. The **declared finite-mode model** of the
species with these data is the declared species sector of clause (a) whose
one-particle space is $K$, together with its $n$-particle sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq K^{\otimes n}$
and the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
clauses (c)-(d). The declaration is an idealization: it asserts that the model
confines the one-particle content to the $d$ declared modes. No claim is made
that a species has finitely many modes; whether the declared modes describe a
laboratory mode family is a tested identification with uncertainty under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a consequence of this definition.

**(c) The occupation readouts.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ let
$$N_j:K^{\otimes n}\to K^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n}\rangle\,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\},$$
be the occupation operator of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (d) for the
basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$. By that clause $N_j$ is bounded and self-adjoint, the
$N_j$ commute pairwise, and $N_j$ preserves the sector $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$;
the **sector occupation readout** is the restriction
$$N_j^\sigma:=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},$$
a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with spectrum
contained in $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The model reads $(N_j^\sigma,\text{particle
count})$ as an assigned sharp observable of the declared sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a):
its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\, E_{N_j^\sigma}(B)\bigr),\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
the reading of P2 clause (ii) through the observable definition.

**(d) The joint occupation readout.** The operators $N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma$
are simultaneously diagonalised by the sector bases of the cited theorem: the
Slater basis in the fermionic case and the family $(m_\lambda)$ in the
bosonic case, with joint eigenvalues $\mathbf 1_J$ and $\lambda$ respectively.
Write $\Lambda_n:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\lambda_j\le n,\
\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ and, for $\lambda\in\Lambda_n$, let $P_\lambda$ be the
orthogonal projection of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ onto the joint eigenspace of
$(N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma)$ for the eigenvalue vector $\lambda$; the cited
theorem exhibits a line $\mathbb C m_\lambda$ for every bosonic
$\lambda\in\Lambda_n$. In the fermionic sector there is a line
$\mathbb C f_J^\wedge$ exactly when $\lambda=\mathbf 1_J$ for an
$n$-element subset $J$; if any entry of $\lambda$ is at least $2$, the joint
eigenspace is $\{0\}$ and $P_\lambda=0$. Thus the $P_\lambda$, including
these zero projections, are mutually orthogonal, their finite sum is the
identity of the sector, and $N_j^\sigma=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
\lambda_jP_\lambda$. The model reads the **joint occupation readout** through
the finite family $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$: the joint law in a
declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)\qquad (\lambda\in\Lambda_n),$$
and the marginal law of $N_j^\sigma$ is recovered by
$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\sum_{\lambda:\lambda_j\in B}\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)$,
because the eigenvalue decomposition of $N_j^\sigma$ groups the $P_\lambda$
by the value $\lambda_j$.

**(e) Total occupation.** By clause (d) of the cited theorem,
$\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; hence the
**total occupation** $\sum_jN_j^\sigma$ has the degenerate outcome law
$\delta_n$ in every declared sector preparation, and the joint law is
supported on $\Lambda_n$: the total number of particles read by the model is
$n$ with certainty.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of the model and
read the cited spectral mathematics through P2; they add no assumption beyond
the sector declaration and the finite-mode idealization of clause (b). The
occupation readouts are sector quantities in the sense of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]];
the exclusion and occupation-count consequences are proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] and
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]]). No measured
count, no detector response, no dynamics and no empirical claim is made.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of effects on $H$ as defined above, with $\sum_aF_a=I$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-$H$ calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt a declared species sector in the vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
the observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) The declared finite-mode model.** Fix $d\ge1$, a finite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $K$ of dimension $d$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with a
declared orthonormal basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, the **declared modes** of the
model, and an integer $n\ge1$. The **declared finite-mode model** of the
species with these data is the declared species sector of clause (a) whose
one-particle space is $K$, together with its $n$-particle sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq K^{\otimes n}$
and the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
clauses (c)-(d). The declaration is an idealization: it asserts that the model
confines the one-particle content to the $d$ declared modes. No claim is made
that a species has finitely many modes; whether the declared modes describe a
laboratory mode family is a tested identification with uncertainty under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a consequence of this definition.

**(c) The occupation readouts.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ let
$$N_j:K^{\otimes n}\to K^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n}\rangle\,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\},$$
be the occupation operator of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (d) for the
basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$. By that clause $N_j$ is bounded and self-adjoint, the
$N_j$ commute pairwise, and $N_j$ preserves the sector $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$;
the **sector occupation readout** is the restriction
$$N_j^\sigma:=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},$$
a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with spectrum
contained in $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The model reads $(N_j^\sigma,\text{particle
count})$ as an assigned sharp observable of the declared sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a):
its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\, E_{N_j^\sigma}(B)\bigr),\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
the reading of P2 clause (ii) through the observable definition.

**(d) The joint occupation readout.** The operators $N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma$
are simultaneously diagonalised by the sector bases of the cited theorem: the
Slater basis in the fermionic case and the family $(m_\lambda)$ in the
bosonic case, with joint eigenvalues $\mathbf 1_J$ and $\lambda$ respectively.
Write $\Lambda_n:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\lambda_j\le n,\
\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ and, for $\lambda\in\Lambda_n$, let $P_\lambda$ be the
orthogonal projection of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ onto the joint eigenspace of
$(N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma)$ for the eigenvalue vector $\lambda$; the cited
theorem exhibits a line $\mathbb C m_\lambda$ for every bosonic
$\lambda\in\Lambda_n$. In the fermionic sector there is a line
$\mathbb C f_J^\wedge$ exactly when $\lambda=\mathbf 1_J$ for an
$n$-element subset $J$; if any entry of $\lambda$ is at least $2$, the joint
eigenspace is $\{0\}$ and $P_\lambda=0$. Thus the $P_\lambda$, including
these zero projections, are mutually orthogonal, their finite sum is the
identity of the sector, and $N_j^\sigma=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
\lambda_jP_\lambda$. The model reads the **joint occupation readout** through
the finite family $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$: the joint law in a
declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)\qquad (\lambda\in\Lambda_n),$$
and the marginal law of $N_j^\sigma$ is recovered by
$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\sum_{\lambda:\lambda_j\in B}\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)$,
because the eigenvalue decomposition of $N_j^\sigma$ groups the $P_\lambda$
by the value $\lambda_j$.

**(e) Total occupation.** By clause (d) of the cited theorem,
$\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; hence the
**total occupation** $\sum_jN_j^\sigma$ has the degenerate outcome law
$\delta_n$ in every declared sector preparation, and the joint law is
supported on $\Lambda_n$: the total number of particles read by the model is
$n$ with certainty.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of the model and
read the cited spectral mathematics through P2; they add no assumption beyond
the sector declaration and the finite-mode idealization of clause (b). The
occupation readouts are sector quantities in the sense of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]];
the exclusion and occupation-count consequences are proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] and
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]]). No measured
count, no detector response, no dynamics and no empirical claim is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

**(a) State space.** Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] for a declared system of the declared massive-matter sector, with its assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. The **state space of the system in the model** is the set
$$D(H)=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}$$
of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]: the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $H$ of trace one. A **state** of the system is an element of $D(H)$; this is the geometry vocabulary for the general preparations of clause (iii) of the state postulate. The model's adopted assignment of a state to each preparation is not produced by this definition; it is the content of that postulate.

**(b) Pure and mixed states.** A state is **pure** when it is one of the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$, and **mixed** when it is not pure, as in [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the map
$$j:R(H)\to D(H),\qquad j([\psi])=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is a bijection of the ray space onto the set of pure states; and by clause (ii) of the state postulate the pure preparations are the unit rays of $H$, so the model's pure preparations are exactly its pure states.

**(c) State assigned to a state vector.** For a nonzero vector $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **state assigned to $\psi$** is the normalized rank-one operator
$$\widehat\rho(\psi)=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}\in D(H),$$
which by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; clause (ii) of the state postulate assigns the same operator to the pure preparation $[\psi]$. The zero vector is excluded here because $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ is defined only for $\psi\ne0$; no state is assigned to it, in agreement with the state postulate.

**(d) Mixtures and purity.** A **statistical mixture** of preparations with weights is the trace-norm convergent sum of clause (iii) of the state postulate; its value is the corresponding convex combination of states. The **purity** of a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})$, and by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]] a state is pure exactly when its purity equals $1$.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) record the readings of the state postulate in the geometry vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. The cited mathematical suppliers of the ray-to-state correspondence and of the purity criterion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is carried as a hypothesis of these readings. They adopt no assumption beyond the state postulate and that hypothesis, assert no dynamics, no probability law and no measurement model, and make no empirical claim: in particular, whether a given laboratory preparation is pure or mixed, and whether a given apparatus realizes a prescribed mixture, are physical identifications with uncertainty, governed by the preparation and apparatus assumptions of the framework, not consequences of this definition. Superselection restrictions and identical-particle symmetry sectors, where imposed, are separate assumptions by clause (v) of the state postulate and are not part of the state space fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H^{\otimes n}$ and
$P_\pm^{(n)}$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] (with
$P_\pm^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$), and let $W(n,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$
and $m_\lambda$ be the symmetric vectors of that theorem. Then:

(a) *fermionic configurations*: the map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection
from the set of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,d\}$ onto the set
$\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$; consequently
$$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\#\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\textstyle\sum_j\lambda_j=n\},\qquad \sum_{n=0}^{d}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=2^{d};$$

(b) *bosonic configurations*: the assignment $\lambda\mapsto m_\lambda$ induces
a bijection from $W(n,d)$ onto the set of lines spanned by the orthogonal basis
$(m_\lambda)$, so the number of bosonic configurations of total occupation
exactly $n$ is $\binom{n+d-1}{n}=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$, and for every $N\ge0$ the
number of bosonic configurations of total occupation at most $N$ is
$$\sum_{n=0}^{N}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{N+d}{d};$$

(c) *exclusion counts*: no fermionic configuration has an entry $\ge2$, so the
antisymmetric Slater index set contains no $\lambda$ with $\lambda_j\ge2$ for
some $j$; for $n>d$ there is no fermionic configuration at all and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$, while for every $n$ and every $j$ the
bosonic configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ and all other entries $0$ occurs, so
no occupation bound holds in the symmetric sector;

(d) *consistency with the total occupation*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ one
has $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$, and for every fermionic configuration
$\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d\cap\{\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ likewise; in particular the
total occupation equals the particle number $n$ in both sectors.

derivations.claim: [Sector restrictions are self-adjoint] By [F1] the operator $N_j$ preserves $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$, and both the Slater family and the family $(m_\lambda)$ consist of eigenvectors of $N_j$ with real eigenvalues and form a basis of the respective sector; a linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space that is diagonal in an orthogonal basis with real eigenvalues is self-adjoint. Hence each $N_j^\sigma=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$, which is the readout declared in clauses (c)-(d) of the model.

[Finite spectral measures and laws] Fix $\sigma\in\{-,+\}$ and $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$. By [F3], the finite family of projections
$$F_j(B):=\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda_n\\\lambda_j\in B}}P_\lambda\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\text{ Borel})$$
is a projection-valued measure: $F_j(\varnothing)=0$ and $F_j(\mathbb R)=I$ because the $P_\lambda$ sum to $I$; each $F_j(B)$ is an orthogonal projection; intersections satisfy $F_j(B\cap C)=F_j(B)F_j(C)$ because the $P_\lambda$ are mutually orthogonal; and countable additivity is strong since only finitely many $\lambda$ occur and the Borel sets in a disjoint sequence contain each eigenvalue $\lambda_j$ at most once. Its scalar measures $\mu_x(B):=\langle F_j(B)x,x\rangle$ are finite and supported on the finite set $S_j:=\{\lambda_j:\lambda\in\Lambda_n\}$, hence regular: for every Borel $B$, the compact set $B\cap S_j$ and an open set $U$ with $U\cap S_j=B\cap S_j$ give $\mu_x(B\cap S_j)=\mu_x(B)=\mu_x(U)$. Its spectral integral is the finite sum
$$\int_{\mathbb R}r\,dF_j(r)=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}\lambda_jP_\lambda=N_j^\sigma.$$
Thus $F_j$ is the spectral PVM of $N_j^\sigma$ by uniqueness of the spectral PVM in [F2]. The outcome law in $\rho$ is therefore $\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_j(B))$. In the fermionic sector [F1] restricts the joint eigenvalue vectors to $\mathbf 1_J\in\{0,1\}^d$, so this spectral measure is supported on $\{0,1\}$; in the symmetric sector it groups the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ by the value $\lambda_j$. This identifies the readout laws of clauses (c)-(d) of the model.

[Exclusion] Assume $\sigma=-$. By step 1.2 the spectral measure of $N_j^-$ is supported on $\{0,1\}$, so $E_{N_j^-}([2,\infty))=0$ and $\mu^{N_j^-}_\rho([2,\infty))=\operatorname{tr}(0)=0$; moreover $N_j^-(N_j^--I)=0$ on the sector because the operator vanishes on the Slater basis by [F1], so its expectation $\operatorname{tr}(\rho N_j^-(N_j^--I))$ is zero. For the joint law, [F1] shows that the joint eigenspaces with an entry $\ge2$ do not occur among the lines $\mathbb Cf_J^\wedge$, so the sum of the corresponding projections $P_\lambda$ is zero and $\mu^{N}_\rho(\{\lambda:\lambda_j\ge2\ \text{for some }j\})=0$. This proves (a).

[Bosonic contrast] Assume $\sigma=+$. For every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is nonzero and spans the joint eigenspace for $\lambda$ by [F1], so $P_\lambda\ne0$; for the pure preparation of the ray of $m_\lambda$ the weight is $\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)=\|P_\lambda x\|^2/\|x\|^2=1$ for any unit representative $x$ of that ray by [F4]. By [F5] the configurations $\lambda$ with $\lambda_j=n$ lie in $W(n,d)$, so they occur; this proves (b).

[Total occupation] By [F1] one has $\sum_jN_j=nI$ on the whole tensor power, hence on the sector, and therefore $\sum_jN_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; since the total occupation is the constant operator $nI$, its outcome law assigns probability one to $\{n\}$ in every preparation, and applying the joint law of [F1] gives $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$ for every configuration of the support; this is (c).

[Assembly and scope] Step 2.1 proves (a), step 2.2 proves (b) and step 2.3 proves (c). The proof is conditional on the declared sector of P6, the declared finite-mode readout and the cited spectral mathematics; no measured occupancy, no apparatus behaviour and no derivation of a species' statistics is asserted.

citations.quote:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator

spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**

[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],

orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density

declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,

with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and

not asserted equivalent to commutation. An

laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let

projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$

eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$), and the joint eigenspaces inside
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (one for each
